evidence_tier: ★ COACHING. This whole artifact is a READING, not a measurement. Every figure it quotes is sourced (◆ deck-facts / deck-audit / goldfish_metrics.json / bracket_report.json, or a checker-passed stack); every framework claim carries the strategy:<id> it came from and the quote is verbatim from that section. A strategy citation never upgrades a line to rules-verified, and no candidate line below is a fact.
mandate: Pilot-approved target bracket 4; the computed FLOOR MOVED DOWN at v1.0.2 to 3 (bracket_report.json: floor 3 'Upgraded' on three Game Changers — Enlightened Tutor, Teferi's Protection, Worldly Tutor — target 4, within_target true). Smothering Tithe was the fourth and the eminence-v3 merge cut it. Bracket 3's own definition is the deck's self-description: strategy:deckbuilding.power-level — "3 Upgraded, strong synergy and one-big-turn kills off accrued resources, at least six". The pilot's standing brief is unchanged: power, consistency and menace, bracket 4 approved, swap freely where the evidence supports it (pilot_feedback.md, 2026-07-28). What is NEW is the brief from the table. log.jsonl 003 (2026-09-01, five-player pod, loss, cause 'politics'): "speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close." That sentence, not the mana, is what this frame is written against.
archetype: Five-colour Dragon typal ramp-into-entry-triggers, re-tuned at v1.0.2 to accelerate: five mana dorks (Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Delighted Halfling, Faeburrow Elder, Ignoble Hierarch), four rocks, five cost reducers stacking under eminence, 21 Dragons in the 99 plus the commander, four per-Dragon damage payoffs and two damage doublers. The eminence-v3 merge bought that speed with the answer suite: Counterspell, Swan Song and Dovin's Veto all left, and an oracle scan of all 96 entries for 'counter target' now returns NOTHING. Written deliberately without an archetype keyword — deck_audit._ARCHETYPE_HINTS keyword-matches this string, and with 30 creature copies and 22 ramp copies the base targets are the right yardstick.

role_assignment.default_role: THE ROLE INVERTED AT v1.0.2 AND THE FRAME IT REPLACES HAD IT THE OTHER WAY ROUND. The v1.0.0 reading was the engine seat that owns the long game, on strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's "four-player games trend long, so inevitability compounds — engines are the default winning plan". That is no longer this deck. strategy:whos-the-beatdown is explicit that "the roles are set by matchup and game state, not your deck's label", and the game state this list now creates is a fast one: ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c gives mean available mana 3.595 / 4.895 / 5.934 on turns three to five (v1.0.0 measured 4.219 at turn five), land drops 0.906 / 0.775 / 0.650, and a median goldfish kill turn of 7 with 0.357 of runs killing by turn six. Apply the metagame-clock's own table test — "picture turn 15 with both players on their best draws — whoever likes that picture less should be attacking now": at turn 15 this deck's picture is a 37-power board it cannot protect and cannot refill (4 card-advantage copies against the ratio floor of 10), so YOU are the one who likes turn 15 less. You are the fast seat from roughly turn four onward. The correction is not to slow down — it is to stop LOOKING fast while you do it (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: "the deflection skill is managing your *perceived* threat level below your actual one"). CAVEAT ON THE GOLDFISH: it has no blockers, no removal and no opponents, so its kill turns are a resource-development ceiling, not a table forecast. Game 003 is the counter-example in one line — the same list, four opponents, no kill at all.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: REDEFINED. v1.0.0's trigger was a board condition alone: a per-Dragon damage payoff plus a widener. That condition is necessary and it is no longer sufficient, because game 003 met it (Miirym + Terror of the Peaks + Gadrak on board, 'two copies of Terror is twenty targeted damage') and still lost. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's bar is a TABLE condition — "protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for" — and "assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing". So the trigger now has two legs and both must be true: (1) BOARD — a per-Dragon damage payoff (Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas) plus a widener (Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm, Lathliss, Dragon Queen, Utvara Hellkite, Ancient Gold Dragon) plus a haste source if the plan needs combat (Temur Ascendancy, Dragon Tempest on a flier, Lightning Greaves, Sneak Attack); and (2) TABLE — open mana counted seat by seat, at least one protection piece in hand and CASTABLE, and the pod's attention on someone else. Leg 2 is the one that failed on 2026-09-01. ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c prices leg 1 at 0.235 assembled / 0.150 by turn six (entry kill) and 0.243 / 0.157 (combat kill); it prices nothing about leg 2, which is the pilot's job at the table. strategy:pivot-point: "hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after".

gameplan_by_phase.turns_1_3: Fixing and acceleration, and this is the phase v1.0.1+v1.0.2 actually fixed. ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c: land drop 0.999 / 0.996 / 0.906 on turns one to three, mean available mana 3.595 by turn three, 'Ramp or fixing drawn' 0.904 assembled with a mean turn of 2.213, mean mulligans 0.246 and 0.884 of keeps able to act by turn three. Game 003 is the anecdote that matches: turn one land into Sol Ring into Arcane Signet, turn two Bloom Tender. Mulligan on strategy:mulligans.engine-hands — "mulligan to the key card", which here means an ENABLER class (a dork, a rock or a reducer), not a Dragon. THE NEW DISCIPLINE FOR THIS PHASE IS SOCIAL: strategy:multiplayer.pod-management notes that "early game watches who is "setting up for the win" with ramp and draw", and strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection warns that "experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player". Four mana on turn one is not invisible. Expect the read, and pre-empt it in words rather than by playing worse.
gameplan_by_phase.turns_4_6: The build phase and the whole decision surface. Mean available mana 4.895 / 5.934 / 6.734, mean bodies 1.383 / 2.350 / 3.251, mean board power 6.325 / 11.698 / 17.404 (◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c). strategy:deckbuilding.curve's instruction is "Build to hit 2, 4 and 6 mana reliably" and this list now does: the modal nonland mana value is 3 (18 of 64) and the six-mana turn arrives on schedule. The trap the pilot named is exactly here — 'I ramped fast enough to broadcast the win before I could actually present lethal'. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection's rule is the fix: "Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress." Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge is a tell (it reads as a Treasure engine and it drew three artifact removals); Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm is a tell; Terror of the Peaks is a tell. Sequence the LEAST frightening enabler first and hold the tell for the turn it converts (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: "sequence the scariest piece last").
gameplan_by_phase.turn_7_plus: Convert or lose the long game. ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c puts the median goldfish kill at turn 7 and 0.655 of runs killing by turn seven — but that model has no blockers, no removal and no politics, and the deck's refuel is 4 card-advantage copies against a ratio floor of 10 (strategy:deckbuilding.ratios via deck-audit). So a game that reaches turn ten with the board answered is a game this deck loses slowly. strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs, read from ahead: "from ahead, count THEIR outs and close them" — count each seat's open mana before the swing, and prefer the line that wins through one answer rather than the line that wins bigger through none (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: "Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail").

With Panharmonicon on board, one Lathliss, Dragon Queen cast makes two nonlegendary 6/6 hasty copies and 64 damage in 12 separately-targeted instances — enough to kill a 32-life seat, and its own final_state records the 40-life seat surviving at 8. WITHOUT Panharmonicon the same cast makes one copy and 20 damage in 4 instances and kills nobody: stack 007 states 'Cutting Panharmonicon costs stack 002 its LETHALITY'. That is the deck's single most load-bearing non-Dragon.

engines.piece: Sneak Attack + Drakuseth, Maw of Flames
engines.engine: The cheat-and-haste lane, and the deck's answer to its own summoning sickness in one card: {R} puts a 7/7 in WITH HASTE, the attack trigger fires for 4+3+3 before blockers, it connects for 7, and all 17 damage stands through the mandatory end-step sacrifice. Its proven limit matters for the pilot's haste research: Sneak Attack cannot touch the command zone, so it is not a route to the nine-mana commander.

engines.piece: The haste layer: Temur Ascendancy, Dragon Tempest, Lightning Greaves, Sneak Attack, Hellkite Courser, Glorybringer, Goldspan Dragon, Smaug the Magnificent
engines.engine: DIRECT ANSWER TO RESEARCH THREADS (a) AND (b), AND THE DECK ALREADY HAS MORE OF THIS THAN THE PILOT THINKS. An oracle scan of all 96 entries for 'haste' returns exactly eight, in four tiers: BOARD-WIDE AND UNCONDITIONAL — Temur Ascendancy, 'Creatures you control have haste', three mana, {G}{U}{R}; BOARD-WIDE ON ENTRY — Dragon Tempest, 'Whenever a creature you control with flying enters, it gains haste until end of turn', which covers 20 of the 21 Dragons in the 99 — an enumeration of the flying keyword over all 96 entries returns 22 names, and the single Dragon MISSING from it is Thrakkus the Butcher (Trample, no flying), while the single non-Dragon flier is Birds of Paradise — and which two checker-passed stacks confirm in practice (stack 001's fifteen tokens enter 'with haste'; stack 002's Lathliss copies are hasty); SINGLE TARGET — Lightning Greaves (equip {0}, haste AND shroud, though shroud also stops YOUR own targeting), Sneak Attack, Hellkite Courser (commander only, returns at end step); PRINTED ON THE BODY — Glorybringer, Goldspan Dragon, Smaug the Magnificent. The gap is not the count, it is that the two board-wide grants are non-Dragon enchantments the deck draws at ordinary rates and that Dragon Tempest's grant is spent the turn the Dragon enters. ONE CORRECTION TO THE THREAD AS WRITTEN: Terror of the Peaks does not need to swing. Its damage is 'Whenever another creature you control enters, this creature deals damage equal to that creature's power to any target' — an entry trigger, not an attack trigger. What haste buys Terror is that the Dragons entering alongside it can also attack; what protects Terror is a different question.
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json, all 96 entries scanned); verified stacks 001, 002, 005

engines.piece: The deterrence layer: Thunderbreak Regent, Terror of the Peaks, Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm
engines.engine: PARTIAL ANSWER TO RESEARCH THREAD (c), AND THE HONEST FINDING IS THAT IT IS A TAX, NOT A LOCK. Thunderbreak Regent: 'Whenever a Dragon you control becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, this creature deals 3 damage to that player.' Terror of the Peaks: 'Spells your opponents cast that target this creature cost an additional 3 life to cast.' Miirym: ward {2}. Enumerated: Thunderbreak and Terror cannot STOP anything, they only price it; ward {2} is the one of the three that does counter the spell, and only when the opponent declines to pay {2}. Each of the three prices removal rather than preventing it. Against one opponent a 3-life tax is real; against four opponents at 40 it is strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's problem in reverse — 'Every single-target card you cast is a net loss against the table' cuts both ways, and a table that has decided you are the archenemy will pay 3 life four times over. Game 003 is the datum: the table converged and the taxes did not deter it.

engines.piece: The protection package: Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Deflecting Swat, Lightning Greaves
engines.engine: THE SHARPEST DISAGREEMENT IN THIS FRAME, AND IT IS WORTH STATING RATHER THAN RESOLVING. deck-audit's protection axis reads 8 copies against strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's "3-5 finishers, "at least 3 finishers in your deck", 5-7 protection slots, 20-25 flexible strategy cards" and calls it 'over'. The PILOT says 'I cut protection and counters for speed, and it showed'. Both are right about different things and the disagreement is the finding. Enumerating the eight: two of them — Miirym (ward {2}) and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus ({1}{R/P}{R/P}, discard two cards, for ONE indestructible counter on itself) — protect only themselves and only barely, which leaves SIX board-protection cards. Of those six, two read 'If you control a commander' (Flawless Maneuver, Deflecting Swat) — and ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c puts the commander on the battlefield by turn six in only 0.329 of runs, median cast turn 7. So on the turns this deck actually pivots, the free protection is usually not free and costs {2}{W} or {2}{R} out of the same mana that casts the Dragon. The measurable shape of the problem is interaction_castable_by_turn: 0.279 / 0.371 / 0.455 on turns four to six — and the model's own note says that figure is a FLOOR, because it casts everything it can afford rather than holding mana up. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance's taxonomy is the frame: Lightning Greaves is the "constant protection (boots-style equipment and enchantments — always on, cheap to re-arm, useless against wraths)" tier and the other five are single-use instants that 'cost held mana all game'. What the deck lacks is not COUNT, it is a protection piece that is on before the pivot turn and does not compete for the pivot turn's mana.
engines.evidence: ◆ deck-audit protection axis (8 copies, verdict 'over'); oracle text for all eight; ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c 'Protection held for the big turn' 0.673 assembled / 0.565 by turn six, commander.cast_by_turn_6_rate 0.329, interaction_castable_by_turn

engines.piece: The damage doublers: Twinflame Tyrant, Solphim, Mayhem Dominus, Thrakkus the Butcher, Atarka, World Render

Twinflame Tyrant doubles ALL damage a source you control deals to an opponent or their permanents; Solphim doubles NONCOMBAT damage only; Thrakkus doubles the POWER of each Dragon when it attacks; Atarka grants an attacking Dragon double strike. Read against the entry cascade, Twinflame and Solphim both multiply Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas triggers, which is the shortest path this list has from 'a board' to 'a table kill'. combo_details has 12 records touching Twinflame Tyrant and 9 touching Solphim and NOT ONE is fully contained in this 99 — so every one of these pairings is a candidate below, not a fact.

engines.piece: Treasure fuel: Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone, Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, Ganax, Astral Hunter, Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge, Smaug the Magnificent

Gadrak's two clauses gate on different things and are worth quoting exactly: 'Gadrak can't attack unless you control four or more artifacts', and separately 'At the beginning of your end step, create a Treasure token for each nontoken creature that died this turn.' With only 8 artifact entries in the 99, an opponent removing three artifacts turns Gadrak off as an attacker — which is what log.jsonl 003 records happening.

key_tensions.tension: Speed against invisibility — the pilot's own headline
key_tensions.reading: v1.0.2 bought turn-five mana (4.219 → 5.934 mean available, ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c) and paid in answers. strategy:critical-mass states the trade flatly — "linear strategies give up flexibility in exchange for power" and "interaction slots are the price of the engine, so the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers" — so the build is COHERENT: this is what a linear deck is supposed to look like. The doc's Commander correction is the bill that came due on 2026-09-01: "the linear deck needs redundancy that shrugs off three answers, or a deflection posture that keeps them unspent". This list has neither leg fully. Redundancy is real on the ENABLER side (five reducers, eight accelerants, 21 Dragons) and thin on the PAYOFF side (four finishers by deck-audit's threat-density count), and the deflection posture is a piloting skill the deck's own speed works against.

key_tensions.tension: Zero stack interaction against a plan that must resolve a six-mana Dragon
key_tensions.reading: An oracle scan of all 96 entries for 'counter target' returns nothing: the v1.0.2 merge cut Counterspell, Swan Song and Dovin's Veto and replaced none of them. deck-audit's interaction-breadth axis reads 4 of 5 classes, verdict 'under', against strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite's "cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any". The same section notes "Answers to answers are a separate budget — Commander Deck Maker: 2-4 protection generic, 4-6 combo, 6-8 Voltron; counterspells do both jobs." — this deck now has the protection budget and none of the double-duty. Consequence at the table: the pivot turn cannot be defended on the stack, only after resolution, which is why the protection package's mana cost is the binding constraint rather than its card count.

key_tensions.tension: Four finishers and one refuel, against a table with three untap steps
key_tensions.reading: deck-audit: card-advantage 4 copies against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' floor of 10, verdict 'under' by six — with the honest caveat the tool itself prints, that Dragon's Hoard, Return of the Wildspeaker, Rishkar's Expertise and Sarkhan, Fireblood show the function in oracle text and are NOT in the count. Even generously read, this deck rebuilds badly. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math is therefore not optional: "assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — so deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package", and its second instruction is the buildable one — "buy resilience instead of restraint where you can".

key_tensions.tension: Black is 12 sources short of its Karsten target and costs almost nothing
key_tensions.reading: deck-audit colour-sources: B 18 have / 30 target (short 12), R 30/36 (short 6), W 19/22, U 20/22, G 23/22. The B target is a Karsten figure computed from the commander's identity, and deck-facts shows what black actually asks for in this list: 3 total pips across 2 cards, earliest turn 5. strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources says to "Read them as a budget, not a table" and that its 99-card column assumes 40 lands 'on the play, casting on curve'. So the 12-source black shortfall is a REPORTING artifact of a five-colour identity, not a deck problem; the 6-source RED shortfall against 52 red pips across 33 cards is the one that is real.

table_politics_layer.note: RESEARCH THREAD (d), answered from the doc rather than from the metaphor. The pilot asked for a Daenerys frame: when you are the one with the dragon army, read the room, form alliances, hold back a swing. The strategy doc has all three ideas and names them differently; below is the mapping, so the pilot's instinct and the doc's vocabulary are the same object. This is ★ coaching in its purest form and none of it is measured.
table_politics_layer.read_the_room: strategy:multiplayer.pod-management is the stage model: "early game watches who is "setting up for the win" with ramp and draw", and midgame 'asks who accomplishes the most per turn and whether their win takes out one player or the table'. Its resource claim is the one to internalise: "Track attention like a resource: after any flashy play, the table's assessment updates", so "spend a turn or two under the radar" after any flashy turn. Read the pod back with strategy:information.range-tells — "Weight inaction heaviest — what they did NOT do with mana available is the strongest signal".
table_politics_layer.manage_what_they_see: strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection: "the deflection skill is managing your *perceived* threat level below your actual one". Concretely for this deck — deploy the accelerant before the payoff, let a rock read as fixing rather than as a clock, and remember "experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player", so the silent-ramp posture is NOT available to you at four mana on turn one. "Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress."
table_politics_layer.form_alliances: strategy:multiplayer.politics: "attention, favors, and perceived threat are spendable currencies". Craft rules that apply directly to a Dragon board — "keep deals small, specific, and expiring" and "never lie outright about game state (credibility is a multi-game resource)" (the pod is Sean's regular table; credibility there is a multi-game asset, and strategy:information.range-tells says the same: "your image persists — a pod remembers which bluffs you run and which fears you exploit"). The operating goal is one sentence: "Position yourself so eliminating you is never anyone's most profitable line until you're winning that turn."
table_politics_layer.hold_back_the_swing: strategy:combat-math's Commander correction is why a full alpha strike is a political act: "combat is also diplomacy — every attack chooses an enemy and opens your defenses to two bystanders". Attacking one seat with everything makes an enemy and opens you to the other three. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection's higher-value alternative: "Forcing opponents to exhaust interaction on each other early is worth more than any single card you could cast." A partial swing that leaves blockers home is a signal AND a defence; a full swing is a declaration.
table_politics_layer.spend_it_at_the_right_moment: strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: "The deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out" and "Go too early and the table unites to stop you with three players' worth of interaction". Game 003 spent the budget on turn-one Sol Ring and an early Gadrak and had none left when the board was finally worth converting. strategy:tempo.sequencing's practical rules: "think through the entire turn before doing anything", "strike in the window when opponents are tapped out and cannot respond", and "prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent".
table_politics_layer.gap: The doc has no section on a deck whose ACCELERATION is the tell. threat-deflection assumes you can look harmless while you build; this deck cannot. Filed in gaps.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Twinflame Tyrant doubling the entry cascade

Stack 001 (checker-passed) puts 255 available damage on the table from Tempest alone at a fixed d20 of 15; nothing has resolved what Solphim does to that number, whether Solphim and Twinflame stack multiplicatively, or how the doubling interacts with each trigger's independently locked-in target. combo_details: 9 records touch Solphim, ZERO fully contained here.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Thrakkus the Butcher turning a token board into lethal commander-less damage
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Thrakkus: 'Whenever Thrakkus attacks, double the power of each Dragon you control until end of turn.' Atarka: 'Whenever a Dragon you control attacks, it gains double strike until end of turn.' Utvara Hellkite makes a 6/6 flier per attacking Dragon. The ordering question is the whole line — Utvara's tokens arrive attacking, after Thrakkus's doubling has already applied — and it decides whether this is a table-kill or a big attack. combo_details has ZERO records for Thrakkus.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Scourge of the Throne's extra combat as a second Utvara/Ur-Dragon trigger
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Scourge of the Throne untaps all attacking creatures and adds an extra combat phase when it attacks the player with the most life. Utvara Hellkite triggers per attacking Dragon, Old Gnawbone makes Treasures equal to the combat damage each of your creatures deals to a player, and the commander draws per attacking Dragon and may put a permanent in. An extra combat runs all three again. Whether the second combat's tokens are attacking, and what 'most life' does in a five-player pod where the totals move, is unresolved. 16 combo_details records touch Scourge of the Throne, ZERO fully contained here.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Firespitter Whelp as a table-wide clock under a doubler
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Firespitter Whelp: 'Whenever you cast a noncreature or Dragon spell, this creature deals 1 damage to each opponent' — the only each-opponent drain in the 99, which is exactly the shape strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry asks for ('~120 combined life behind three defenses makes incremental combat damage a losing plan'). Under Solphim or Twinflame that is 2 per spell to every seat. Whether the doublers apply once per opponent, and what a realistic spell count per turn is here, needs resolving. combo_details has ZERO records for Firespitter Whelp.

candidate_missing_lines.title: Temur Ascendancy making the pivot turn a one-turn kill
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: RESEARCH THREAD (a)/(b) AS A LINE RATHER THAN A SHOPPING LIST. Temur Ascendancy grants unconditional board-wide haste, so a Dragon and its Miirym copy can attack the turn they land — which is what makes Utvara's per-attacking-Dragon tokens and Thrakkus's doubling reachable in one turn instead of two. It also draws a card per power-4-or-greater arrival. No stack has ever resolved a hasted Miirym cascade, and the goldfish cannot answer it: its combat model has no blockers.

matchup_frames.vs_the_converged_table: THE MATCHUP THIS DECK ACTUALLY LOST, AND IT IS NOT AN OPPONENT — IT IS A STATE. log.jsonl 003: 'once the table read "Sean is swinging for 28 in the air" they converged immediately'. strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window names the mechanism — "Go too early and the table unites to stop you with three players' worth of interaction" — and strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection names the cure — "The deflection budget spends down as your engine shows; plan the pivot before it runs out". Three concrete rules for this list. (1) The tell is the RAMP, not the Dragon: at four mana on turn one you are already the player strategy:multiplayer.pod-management says the table watches, so open the conversation about someone else's board before yours is worth talking about. (2) Do not cast the piece whose text answers 'how does he win' until the turn it wins — "Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress." Gadrak was cast a turn early and drew three artifact removals; the deck has 8 artifact entries and Gadrak 'can't attack unless you control four or more artifacts'. (3) When convergence has already happened, stop presenting and start pricing: strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's "held answers rot" cuts the other way here — the table's answers do not rot, they arrive, so the win attempt must survive one answer rather than beat zero (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: "Prefer win attempts that leave a rebuilt position if they fail").
matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: You are the fast seat and they are the inevitability seat, which is the reverse of the v1.0.0 reading. strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math is the whole plan: "assume the wrath — over a four-player game one is near-certain — so deploy in waves, hold a rebuild package". This deck is well equipped for the first half and badly equipped for the second — Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver and Boros Charm each cover the WHOLE board rather than one permanent, and Miirym and Lathliss rebuild in tokens; but the refuel is 4 counted card-advantage copies against a floor of 10 (deck-audit, verdict 'under'), so a wipe that lands with your hand empty is close to terminal. Deploy in waves. The specific error is jamming the payoff before the widener: the entry board is worth nearly nothing with one leg, so Dragon Tempest resolved into open mana buys THEIR best turn. And note what changed at v1.0.2: with zero counterspells you can no longer stop the wrath, only survive it — which makes the protection card in hand a prerequisite for committing, not a bonus (strategy:pivot-point: "hold the protection spell for the turn you commit, not after").
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Role is forced. strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial: "you rarely own the long game under an assembling lock, so you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion". Taxes hit this deck where it is thinnest — 21 of the 64 nonland entries cost five or more (deck-facts curve: 10 at 5, 5 at 6, 4 at 7, 1 at 8, 1 at 9), against 5.934 mean mana at turn five — but eminence and four printed reducers are a structural discount that a Sphere effect does not remove, and the five mana dorks recover a tax faster than lands do. Name the piece that beats YOU rather than the scariest piece. THE HONEST WEAKNESS IS NEW: with Counterspell, Swan Song and Dovin's Veto cut, nothing in the 99 answers a lock piece on the way in, and strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite says exactly why that matters — 'a counter answers a lock piece only on the way in, so some answers must be castable under the tax'. What remains castable under a tax is Generous Gift, Swords to Plowshares and Chaos Warp. ONE DIRECTION STAYS CLOSED BY THE PILOT: log.jsonl 001 lost to a turn-two Blood Moon; the pilot's recorded decision is that this is an accepted risk and they are not building around it. This frame records that and prescribes nothing against it.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: The matchup where 30 creature copies do defensive work for free, and where strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry's warning — "~120 combined life behind three defenses makes incremental combat damage a losing plan" — is the OPPONENT's problem. 20 of the 21 Dragons in the 99 fly, so they block anything and are blocked by little. The risk is the mirror of the sweeper matchup: an early attacker makes you spend the protection you were holding for the pivot turn, and the removal suite is 9 copies, 7 of them damage-based. strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy's discipline applies — "the bar is "ends the game or ends my deck's function," not "looks scary"" — and a 5/5 Dragon token chump-blocking is cheaper than a card. Do not race: ◆ goldfish, 10,000 iterations, decklist_sha256 5611a822851c puts mean board power at 11.698 on turn five, which is a defensive board before it is an offensive one, and that model has no blockers on either side.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: The clock reading inverts and the deck has no lever. strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's table test — "picture turn 15 with both players on their best draws — whoever likes that picture less should be attacking now" — says attack now; and with zero cards that answer a spell on the stack there is no second plan. The line is to present the entry board early and pay the deflection cost (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection), while using the one lever that still works at instant speed: Deflecting Swat, free if you control a commander, changes the target of a spell or ability with a single target — which answers a targeted tutor-chain piece or a removal spell aimed at your payoff, but not a storm turn. strategy:multiplayer.pod-management's "Leaving instant-speed mana open forces three players, not one, to respect your possible interaction." is worth more here than anywhere else, precisely BECAUSE the deck's open mana is now a bluff (strategy:information.range-tells).

distribution_notes: ◆ deck-facts, deck-audit and goldfish_metrics.json, all at decklist_sha256 5611a822851c. 96 entries / 100 copies; 36 land copies across 32 land entries; 64 nonland. Curve over the 64 nonland entries: 1:7, 2:10, 3:18, 4:8, 5:10, 6:5, 7:4, 8:1, 9:1 — modal 3, and 21 entries at mana value five or more, against strategy:deckbuilding.curve's observed format shape of ~1.5 cards at 8+ and its clock warning that "you're probably only going to be able to cast ONE big-mana spell per game". Creatures 30 copies, of which 21 are Dragons in the 99 (22 Dragon creature entries including the commander); 20 of the 21 fly, the exception being Thrakkus the Butcher. LANDS: 36 copies against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' 36-38 (verdict 'at') and 50 mana sources against the Burgess floor — "lands = 31 + colours in the commander's identity + the commander's mana value, counting 0-mana rocks as lands" — of 45 (verdict 'at'). Only ONE land enters tapped unconditionally (Path of Ancestry) against Duke's "around eight taplands is comfortable in a slow deck, near zero in an aggressive one"; eleven more are shocks or conditional duals, and deck-facts' coarser enters_tapped count of 12 is that superset. COLOUR: sources have/target B 18/30, G 23/22, R 30/36, U 20/22, W 19/22 on Karsten's basis — "his 99-card column assumes 40 lands, on the play, casting on curve, "consistently" ≈ 90%". Pip load is lopsided the same way: R 52 pips over 33 cards, G 21/19, W 11/10, U 4/4, B 3/2 across 2 cards earliest turn 5. Six sources produce RESTRICTED mana that cannot pay a coloured ACTIVATION cost (Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Desolation of Smaug, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Sarkhan, Fireblood, Unclaimed Territory), which is why they accelerate toward casting a Dragon without accelerating what the board then does. ROLES (card_roles covers 96.9%; Chaos Warp, Rishkar's Expertise and Sneak Attack have no pattern): 30 threat:body, 12 utility:activated, 8 ramp:dork, 7 protection:self, 7 removal:damage, 7 value:etb, 6 ramp:treasure, 5 ramp:cost-reduction, 5 threat:tokens, 5 tutor:narrow, 4 ramp:rock, 4 wincon:combat, 4 buff:pump, 3 payoff:typal, 2 removal:spot, 2 ramp:land, 1 removal:sweeper, 1 doubler:triggers — and ZERO counterspell, which was 3 at v1.0.0. AXES THAT MISS: card-advantage 4 vs 10 ('under', with four uncounted oracle-visible sources named by the tool), interaction-breadth 4 of 5 classes ('under'), colour-sources short by 12 in B and 6 in R. AXES OVER: ramp 22 vs 10-12, protection 8 vs 5-7. GOLDFISH (10,000 iterations, model has NO blockers, NO removal and NO opponents — a resource ceiling, not a table forecast): land drops 0.999/0.996/0.906/0.775/0.650 turns 1-5; mean available mana 3.595/4.895/5.934/6.734 turns 3-6; commander cast by turn six 0.329, median cast turn 7; interaction castable 0.279/0.371/0.455 turns 4-6 (a FLOOR by the model's own note); mean mulligans 0.246, 0.884 of keeps able to act by turn three; median goldfish kill turn 7.
overall_assessment: THIS DECK CHANGED ITS ROLE AND HAS NOT YET CHANGED ITS POSTURE, AND THAT GAP IS WHAT LOST GAME 003. v1.0.1 and v1.0.2 did what they set out to do — the mana is fixed on every measure the bench has (36 lands, 50 sources, one unconditional tapland, turn-five mean mana 4.219 → 5.934, and the pilot's own turn-one Sol Ring into Arcane Signet), and the pilot's first diagnosis from log 001, 'the bottleneck is mana consistency', is now discharged. What replaced it is the problem strategy:critical-mass predicts word for word: "linear strategies give up flexibility in exchange for power", "interaction slots are the price of the engine, so the deck's defense is speed, redundancy, and resilience, not answers", and the Commander correction that is now this deck's whole open question — "the linear deck needs redundancy that shrugs off three answers, or a deflection posture that keeps them unspent". v1.0.2 bought speed with the answer suite: three counterspells gone, an oracle scan of all 96 entries returning nothing for 'counter target', interaction-breadth down to 4 of 5 classes, and the computed bracket floor down from 4 to 3 because Smothering Tithe went with them. The deck now reaches a converting board a full turn earlier and can defend it a full tier worse. So the frame's headline is a ROLE REASSIGNMENT, not a card list. Under strategy:whos-the-beatdown — "the roles are set by matchup and game state, not your deck's label" — this is no longer the engine seat that owns the long game; it is the fast seat that must convert before the table's late game arrives, and strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock's turn-15 test says so plainly given 4 card-advantage copies against a floor of 10. Everything the pilot asked for follows from that one reassignment. HASTE (threads a and b) is not absent — eight entries carry it, including Temur Ascendancy's unconditional board-wide grant and Dragon Tempest's grant to entering fliers, which two checker-passed stacks show working — so the real question is not 'add haste' but 'which of the four token-and-copy boards actually converts in one turn', and that is a resolve-stack question, listed in candidate_missing_lines. PROTECTION (thread c) is not a count problem: deck-audit reads 8 copies and calls it over, and the pilot is still right, because two of the eight protect only themselves and two more are free only while you control a commander that arrives by turn six in 0.329 of goldfish runs. The buildable version of thread (c) is strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance's "constant protection (boots-style equipment and enchantments — always on, cheap to re-arm, useless against wraths)" tier — always-on, cheap to re-arm, competing for no mana on the pivot turn. Enumerating that tier over all 96 entries — every Equipment or Enchantment whose text grants hexproof, indestructible, shroud, ward or protection — returns exactly one card, Lightning Greaves, whose shroud also blocks your own targeting. POLITICS (thread d) is the one the doc answers most completely and the one no card can fix: strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection's "the deflection skill is managing your *perceived* threat level below your actual one", strategy:multiplayer.politics' "Position yourself so eliminating you is never anyone's most profitable line until you're winning that turn.", and strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window's "Go too early and the table unites to stop you with three players' worth of interaction" are, between them, an exact description of what happened at Oliver's on 2026-09-01. The one-line world-view: this is a linear Dragon deck whose threshold now arrives around turn five and whose defence of that threshold is a piloting skill and six situational cards — so the next correction is not more speed and probably not more Dragons, it is either always-on protection that costs nothing on the pivot turn, or a deliberate deflection posture that keeps the table's removal pointed elsewhere until the turn the board converts. ★ This whole reading is coaching; the figures inside it are sourced, and not one of the six candidate lines is a fact.
gaps: HASTE AND SUMMONING SICKNESS AS A RESOURCE. Queried five ways ('haste and summoning sickness tempo', 'haste enabling an attacker the turn it lands', …) and the doc returns tempo, sequencing and threat-deflection — none of which mentions haste at all. There is no section on what a turn of summoning sickness costs, when a haste grant is worth a card, or how board-wide haste changes a token strategy's clock. This is the pilot's research thread (a)+(b) and the frame had to derive it from oracle text. RESEARCH TOPIC.

THE DECK WHOSE ACCELERATION IS ITS TELL. strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection assumes you can look harmless while building ('deploy engines that read as defensive') and warns that 'experienced tables hit the quiet ramp player' — but it has no advice for the deck that puts four mana on the table on turn one and cannot be quiet. A section on deliberately slow-rolling acceleration, and on what to say when the table has already read you, is missing. RESEARCH TOPIC (pilot thread d).

A BUILD-SIDE BUDGET FOR BEING THE ARCHENEMY. The doc splits cleanly into play-side politics (threat-deflection, politics, pod-management) and build-side counts (threat-density's 5-7 protection slots, interaction-suite's 2-4 protection generic). Nothing joins them: how many slots a deck should spend because its plan MAKES it the target, as opposed to because removal exists. This deck's audit reads 'protection over' and its pilot reads 'protection short', and the doc cannot arbitrate. RESEARCH TOPIC.

ALWAYS-ON PROTECTION THAT DOES NOT COST A THREAT SLOT. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance has Cullen's taxonomy and prices insurance for a COMMANDER; this deck's engine is a BOARD and its commander is incidental (cast by turn six in 0.329 of runs). Nothing addresses protecting a board of entry-trigger permanents, or the equipment/enchantment question the pilot asked in thread (c). RESEARCH TOPIC.

NONCOMBAT DAMAGE AS A KILL AXIS, AND HOW DOUBLERS COMPOSE. The doc's combat-math tree covers combat and racing; there is no section on trigger-based noncombat damage as a win condition, which is what Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas, Firespitter Whelp, Solphim and Twinflame Tyrant collectively are. Six candidate lines below rest on it. RESEARCH TOPIC.

A COMMANDER THAT IS A STATIC ABILITY RATHER THAN A CARD. Carried forward unresolved from the v1.0.0 frame and still true at v1.0.2: eminence does all the work from the command zone, the nine-mana body arrives in a minority of games, and the doc's archetype-selection and commander-insurance sections both assume the commander is a permanent you are trying to keep. The right advice may simply be that this is fine, and the frame has to argue it from first principles.

Carried forward, unchanged and still unanswered: the basic-land floor for a five-colour deck running Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim — 8 basic land COPIES in the 99 across 4 basic types (4 Mountain, 2 Forest, 1 Island, 1 Plains; no Swamp) — and a Commander-denominated tapland budget — the doc holds Duke's 'around eight taplands' and Karsten's cap 'at about four', which disagree by a factor of two and neither of which is denominated for a 36-land five-colour list.

open_questions.question: Does Twinflame Tyrant double each of stack 002's twelve damage instances, and does that board reach a 40-life seat?
Do Solphim and Twinflame Tyrant compose multiplicatively on a Dragon Tempest trigger, and does Solphim's 'noncombat' clause cover entry-trigger damage?
With Temur Ascendancy on board, can a single Miirym-copied Dragon cast convert in one turn — attacking tokens, Utvara triggers, Thrakkus doubling — and what is the ceiling?
What does the strategy doc say about haste, summoning sickness, and the archenemy build budget? Nothing today; four sections are missing.

Is the card-advantage axis really 'under', or is the taxonomy blind here? deck-audit names Dragon's Hoard, Return of the Wildspeaker, Rishkar's Expertise and Sarkhan, Fireblood as oracle-visible and uncounted.
How much does the protection package actually cost on the pivot turn? interaction_castable_by_turn is a floor by construction; a goldfish run that HOLDS two mana would price it.
